methodological_rigor.justification: Preclinical study combining in vitro co-culture (HT-29, MC38-OVA), in vivo syngeneic MC38 in BALB/c and nude mice, splenocyte ELISpot, and a small clinical correlation (11 CRC patients on ICI, 5 responders vs 6 non-responders). Strengths: explicit T-cell dependency test (nude mice negative), dose-response in vitro, combination-treatment arm vs monotherapies, appropriate ANOVA/Kruskal-Wallis with post-hoc testing, Shapiro-Wilk normality testing, randomization and isotype controls in vivo. Weaknesses: small clinical cohort (n=11) for biomarker claim, intratumoral Exe-9 administration not translatable, no flow-cytometry characterization of T-cell subsets/exhaustion (acknowledged), no in vivo depletion of CD8+ T cells to confirm T-cell dependence beyond nude-mouse model, no independent validation of clinical biomarker finding. Sample size n=10/group is reasonable but no power calculation.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Predominantly preclinical (cell line + mouse models), mapping to Oxford LoE 5. Clinical relevance is meaningful because MSS CRC is poorly responsive to ICIs and GLP-1R antagonism has a plausible T-cell co-stimulatory mechanism, and authors provide a preliminary human biomarker correlation (high GLP-1R in non-responders). However, the translational distance is substantial: intratumoral dosing, no toxicology, and no systemic-route feasibility demonstration. Near-term clinical applicability is speculative.

reporting_quality.justification: ARRIVE applies for the animal component and is largely followed: species/strain, age/weight, housing conditions, randomization, group sizes, drug doses and schedule, endpoints, humane endpoints, and euthanasia method are reported. Cell-line authentication source is stated (Mirror Point Shanghai). Minor gaps: no explicit ARRIVE checklist reference, no formal sample-size calculation justification for n=10, some supplementary table referenced for primers but not reproduced. In vivo H-score methodology and inter-observer adjudication for IHC are clearly described. Antibody catalog numbers are provided.

novelty_literature.justification: Authors claim this is the first direct evidence that combining a GLP-1R antagonist with anti-PD-1 produces synergistic antitumor effect in CRC. Prior work (Ben Nasr et al. 2024, ref 38) established GLP-1R as a T cell-negative costimulatory molecule; Rode et al. 2022 (ref 26) demonstrated functional GLP-1R on T cells. The novel combination with anti-PD-1 in CRC, plus a preliminary biomarker correlation in human samples, constitutes a meaningful novel combinatorial therapeutic hypothesis. Novelty leniency guarded: the GLP-1R-T-cell immunomodulation concept was pre-existing, but the combination-with-ICI demonstration in CRC is a new extension.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is well organized with a logical flow from in vitro to in vivo to clinical correlation. Figures are referenced systematically. Statistical reporting is complete with p-values and correlation coefficients. Limitations are explicitly acknowledged (small sample, TCGA low signal, flow cytometry gap, intratumoral route). Minor issues: typo 'ex2pression' in abstract; some sentences are long; some methods subsections (e.g., ELISA antibody descriptions) include awkward phrasing with nested parentheses.

key_strengths: Multi-tiered preclinical evidence (in vitro T-cell cytotoxicity + in vivo MC38 model + nude-mouse T-cell-dependency test + ELISpot + combination with anti-PD-1) supporting GLP-1R antagonism as a T-cell-mediated mechanism
Explicit test of T-cell dependency via nude-mouse model rescue
Preliminary clinical biomarker correlation: higher GLP-1R in ICI non-responders (n=6) vs responders (n=5) across qPCR, IHC, and Western blot
Novel combinatorial concept: GLP-1R antagonist + anti-PD-1 in CRC
Transparent limitations section addressing small sample, intratumoral route, and lack of flow cytometry
key_concerns: Clinical cohort is very small (n=11) for biomarker claim; no validation set
Intratumoral Exe-9 administration is not clinically translatable; no systemic-route pharmacokinetics or efficacy shown
No CD8+ T-cell depletion experiment to confirm T-cell dependence in immunocompetent mice beyond nude-mouse model
No flow cytometry characterization of T-cell activation/exhaustion (acknowledged limitation)
chief_reviewer.rationale: A well-designed preclinical combination-immunotherapy study with a plausible mechanism and preliminary human correlation, limited by small clinical sample and non-translatable dosing route; fits a mid-tier specialty oncology journal after minor revisions.
